title.zh: 卷一百四十六 列傳第三十三: 耶律楚材 粘合重山 楊惟中
title.en: Volume 146 Biographies 33: Yelü Chucai, Zhanhezhongshan, Yang Weizhong
title.raw: 卷一百四十六 列傳第三十三: 耶律楚材 粘合重山 楊惟中 Volume 146 Biographies 33: Yelü Chucai, Zhanhezhongshan, Yang Weizhong

sentences.zh: 耶律楚材子鑄附

translations.literal: Appendix on Yelü Chucai's son Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: An appendix concerning Yelü Chucai's son Zhu.

sentences.zh: 耶律楚材，字晉卿，遼東丹王突欲八世孫。

translations.literal: Yelü Chucai, styled Jinqing, was an eighth-generation descendant of Yelü Tuyu, King of Dongdan of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Chucai, whose courtesy name was Jinqing, was a great-great-grandson in the eighth generation of Yelü Tuyu, the Liao Prince of Dongdan.

sentences.zh: 父履，以學行事金世宗，特見親任，終尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His father Lü, by his learning and conduct served Emperor Shizong of Jin, was especially favored and trusted, and ended as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lü won the special trust of Jin Emperor Shizong through learning and integrity, rose to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and served him to the end.

sentences.zh: 楚材生三歲而孤，母楊氏教之學。

translations.literal: Chucai was orphaned at three; his mother, née Yang, taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai lost his father when he was three, and his mother, Lady Yang, saw to his education.

sentences.zh: 及長，博極群書，旁通天文、地理、律曆、術數及釋老、醫卜之說，下筆為文，若宿構者。

translations.literal: When grown, he exhausted all books, and broadly mastered astronomy, geography, calendrics, numerology, and the teachings of Buddhism, Daoism, medicine, and divination; when he took up the brush to write, it was as if long prepared.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he read widely across the classics and also mastered astronomy, geography, calendrics, divination, Buddhist and Daoist thought, medicine, and prognostication; his compositions read as though he had drafted them long in advance.

sentences.zh: 金制，宰相子例試補省掾。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, sons of chief ministers were by precedent examined and appointed as provincial clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin law, the sons of chief ministers were routinely examined and appointed as provincial clerks.

sentences.zh: 楚材欲試進士科，章宗詔如舊制。

translations.literal: Chucai wished to sit for the jinshi examination; Emperor Zhangzong decreed that the old system be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai wanted to compete in the jinshi civil examination, and Emperor Zhangzong ordered that the former rules be applied.

sentences.zh: 問以疑獄數事，時同試者十七人，楚材所對獨優，遂辟為掾。

translations.literal: He was questioned on several doubtful legal cases; at the time seventeen sat the examination together, and Chucai's answers alone were superior, whereupon he was appointed a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was tested with several knotty criminal cases; of the seventeen candidates sitting the exam that day, only Chucai's answers stood out, and he was appointed a clerk.

sentences.zh: 後仕為開州同知。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，宣宗遷汴，完顏福興行尚書事，留守燕，辟為左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Wanyan Fuxing acted as Director of the Department of State Affairs, remained to hold Yan, and appointed him Outer Vice Director of the Left and Right Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong relocated to Bian, Wanyan Fuxing stayed behind in Yan as acting director of the Department of State Affairs and recruited Chucai as outer vice director of the left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕，聞其名，召見之。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yan, he heard his name and summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured Yan, he heard of Chucai and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 楚材身長八尺，美髯宏聲。

translations.literal: Chucai was eight feet tall, with a fine beard and a resonant voice.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai stood eight feet tall, with a splendid beard and a booming voice.

sentences.zh: 帝偉之，曰：「遼、金世仇，朕為汝雪之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor thought him imposing and said, "Liao and Jin are hereditary enemies; I will avenge you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his presence and said, "Liao and Jin have been enemies for generations; I will settle that score for you."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣父祖嘗委質事之，既為之臣，敢仇君耶！」

translations.literal: He replied, "My father and grandfather once pledged themselves to serve them; having become their subjects, how dare I bear enmity toward my ruler!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai answered, "My father and grandfather once pledged themselves to Jin; once one has served as a subject, how can one turn against one's sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 帝重其言，處之左右，遂呼楚材曰吾圖撒合里而不名，吾圖撒合裡，蓋國語長髯人也。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued his words, kept him at his side, and thereafter called Chucai Uqtu Saqal rather than by name; Uqtu Saqal means, in the national language, "long-bearded man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected this reply, kept him close, and thereafter called him Uqtu Saqal instead of by his personal name—"long-bearded man" in Mongolian.

sentences.zh: 己卯夏六月，帝西討回回國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the year jimao, the Emperor campaigned west against the Huihui state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the jimao year, the emperor marched west to attack the Muslim realms.

sentences.zh: 祃旗之日，雨雪三尺，帝疑之，楚材曰：「玄冥之氣，見於盛夏，克敵之徵也。」

translations.literal: On the day the war banners were consecrated, rain and snow fell three feet deep; the Emperor was doubtful, and Chucai said, "The qi of the Dark Ultimate appearing in high summer is a sign of overcoming the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: On the day the war banners were consecrated, snow piled three feet deep; when the emperor was troubled by the omen, Chucai said, "Yin force manifesting in midsummer is a sign that the enemy will be overcome."

sentences.zh: 庚辰冬，大雷，復問之，對曰：「回回國主當死於野。」

translations.literal: In winter of the year gengchen there was great thunder; he was asked again and replied, "The lord of the Huihui state will die in the wild."
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the gengchen year there was a great thunderstorm; asked again, he replied, "The ruler of the Muslim lands will die in the field."

sentences.zh: 後皆驗。

translations.literal: Later all were verified.
translations.idiomatic: In time both predictions proved true.

sentences.zh: 夏人常八斤，以善造弓見知於帝，因每自矜曰：「國家方用武，耶律儒者何用。」

translations.literal: The Xia man Chang Bajin, known to the Emperor for skill in bow-making, therefore often boasted, saying, "The state is now employing force—of what use is a Yelü scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang Bajin, a man from Xia famed for his bow-making, would boast, "The realm is at war—what use is a Yelü scholar?"

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「治弓尚須用弓匠，為天下者豈可不用治天下匠耶？」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "Even in making bows one still needs a bowyer; in ruling the realm, how can one not employ those who know how to govern the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai replied, "Even bow-making needs a bowyer—how can ruling the realm do without men who know how to govern it?"

sentences.zh: 帝聞之甚喜，日見親用。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard this with great delight and daily drew him closer in favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and relied on him more closely each day.

sentences.zh: 西域歷人奏五月望夜月當蝕，楚材曰：「否。」

translations.literal: A Western Regions calendrical expert reported that on the night of the full moon in the fifth month there would be a lunar eclipse; Chucai said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: A calendrical expert from the Western Regions reported that the moon would be eclipsed on the night of the fifth-month full moon; Chucai said, "No."

sentences.zh: 卒不蝕。

translations.literal: In the end there was no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: No eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，楚材言月當蝕，西域人曰不蝕，至期果蝕八分。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year Chucai said the moon would be eclipsed; the Western Regions men said it would not; when the time came it was indeed eclipsed eight-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the tenth month, Chucai predicted an eclipse while the Western experts denied it; on the appointed night the moon was eclipsed eight-tenths of its disk.

sentences.zh: 壬午八月，長星見西方，楚材曰：「女直將易主矣。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the year renwu a long comet appeared in the west; Chucai said, "The Jurchen will soon change rulers."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the renwu year a long comet appeared in the west; Chucai said, "The Jurchen throne is about to change hands."

sentences.zh: 明年，金宣宗果死。

translations.literal: The next year Jin Emperor Xuanzong indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jin Emperor Xuanzong did in fact die.

sentences.zh: 帝每征討，必命楚材卜，帝亦自灼羊胛，以相符應。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor campaigned, he invariably ordered Chucai to divine; the Emperor also scorched sheep shoulder-blades himself, to compare the responses.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign the emperor had Chucai cast auguries, while he himself scorched sheep shoulder-blades to see whether the signs agreed.

sentences.zh: 指楚材謂太宗曰：「此人天賜我家。

translations.literal: Pointing to Chucai he said to Taizong, "This man Heaven has bestowed on our house.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to Chucai, he told Taizong, "Heaven has given this man to our house.

sentences.zh: 爾後軍國庶政，當悉委之。」

translations.literal: Hereafter in military and civil affairs of every sort you should wholly entrust them to him."
translations.idiomatic: From now on you should entrust all military and civil business to him."

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝至東印度，駐鐵門關，有一角獸，形如鹿而馬尾，其色綠，作人言，謂侍衛者曰：「汝主宜早還。」

translations.literal: In the year jiashen the Emperor reached Eastern India and halted at Iron Gate Pass; there was a horned beast, shaped like a deer but with a horse's tail, green in color, speaking in human speech, and saying to the guards, "Your lord should return soon."
translations.idiomatic: In the jiashen year the emperor reached eastern India and camped at Iron Gate Pass, where a horned beast like a deer with a horse's tail, green in color, spoke to the guards in human language: "Your lord should turn back soon."

sentences.zh: 帝以問楚材，對曰：「此瑞獸也，其名角端，能言四方語，好生惡殺，此天降符以告陛下。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Chucai, who replied, "This is an auspicious beast; its name is Jiaoduan; it can speak the languages of the four quarters, loves life and hates killing—this is a sign sent down from Heaven to inform Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Chucai, who answered, "This is an auspicious beast called Jiaoduan; it speaks every tongue, loves life and abhors slaughter—it is Heaven's sign to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下天之元子，天下之人，皆陛下之子，願承天心，以全民命。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Heaven's eldest son; all the people under Heaven are Your Majesty's children; I hope you will follow Heaven's mind and thereby preserve the lives of the people."
translations.idiomatic: You are Heaven's firstborn; all under Heaven are your children. I pray you heed Heaven's will and spare the lives of the people."

sentences.zh: 帝即日班師。

translations.literal: The Emperor that same day withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew his army that very day.

sentences.zh: 丙戌冬，從下靈武，諸將爭取子女金帛，楚材獨收遺書及大黃藥材。

translations.literal: In winter of the year bingxu, following the reduction of Lingwu, the generals vied to seize women, children, gold, and silk; Chucai alone collected abandoned books and rhubarb medicinal materials.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the bingxu year, when Lingwu fell, the generals scrambled for women, children, gold, and silk, while Chucai alone gathered abandoned books and stores of rhubarb.

sentences.zh: 既而士卒病疫，得大黃輒愈。

translations.literal: Before long the soldiers fell ill with epidemic disease; those who obtained rhubarb were at once cured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an epidemic swept the army, and those who received rhubarb recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 帝自經營西土，未暇定制，州郡長吏，生殺任情，至孥人妻女，取貨財，兼土田。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had been engaged in the Western Regions and had not yet had leisure to establish regulations, prefectural and district chiefs killed or spared at will, even dragging off men's wives and daughters, seizing goods and wealth, and annexing fields and lands.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was occupied in the west, no fixed laws yet governed the realm; local magistrates killed at whim, seized men's wives and daughters, plundered property, and seized fields.

sentences.zh: 燕薊留後長官石抹咸得卜尤貪暴，殺人盈市。

translations.literal: Shimo Xiandebo, chief magistrate and acting prefect of Yan and Ji, was especially greedy and violent, and killings filled the market.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Xiandebo, the acting prefect of Yan and Ji, was especially rapacious and violent, and the markets ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 楚材聞之泣下，即入奏，請禁州郡，非奉璽書，不得擅徵發，囚當大辟者必待報，違者罪死，於是貪暴之風稍戢。

translations.literal: Chucai wept on hearing this and at once entered to memorialize, requesting that prefectures and districts be forbidden, without an imperial edict bearing the seal, to levy or dispatch on their own authority, and that prisoners liable to capital punishment must await report before execution—violators to be punished by death; thereby the wind of greed and violence was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai wept when he heard of it and immediately memorialized the throne: no prefecture might levy troops or funds without an imperial edict; capital cases must await imperial approval on pain of death for the official. The worst abuses eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 燕多劇賊，未夕，輒曳牛車指富家，取其財物，不與則殺之。

translations.literal: Yan had many fierce bandits; before evening they would drag ox-carts to wealthy houses, take their goods and wealth, and kill them if they did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was overrun with violent robbers who, before nightfall, would drive ox-carts to wealthy homes, seize their goods, and kill anyone who resisted.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗以皇子監國，事聞，遣中使偕楚材往窮治之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Ruizong was supervising the state as imperial son; when the matter was reported, he sent a palace envoy together with Chucai to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong was then regent as imperial son; when word reached him, he sent a palace envoy with Chucai to investigate to the end.

sentences.zh: 楚材詢察得其姓名，皆留後親屬及勢家子，盡捕下獄。

translations.literal: Chucai inquired and ascertained their names; all were relatives of the acting prefect and sons of powerful families; he arrested them all and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai traced the culprits: all were kin of the acting prefect or sons of powerful families; he had every one of them arrested.

sentences.zh: 其家賂中使，將緩之，楚材示以禍福，中使懼，從其言，獄具，戮十六人於市，燕民始安。

translations.literal: Their families bribed the palace envoy, who was about to relax the case; Chucai showed him the consequences of fortune and misfortune; the envoy feared and followed his counsel; when the case was concluded sixteen were executed in the market, and the people of Yan were at last at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Their families bribed the envoy to soften the case, but Chucai showed him what gain and ruin would follow; frightened, the envoy agreed. Sixteen were executed in the market, and the people of Yan were finally at ease.

sentences.zh: 己丑秋，太宗將即位，宗親咸會，議猶未決。

translations.literal: In autumn of the jichou year, as Taizong was about to ascend the throne, the imperial kinsmen all assembled, but deliberation was still unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the jichou year, as Taizong was about to take the throne, the imperial kinsmen all gathered, yet no decision had been reached.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗為太宗親弟，故楚材言於睿宗曰：「此宗社大計，宜早定。」

translations.literal: At the time Prince Ruizong was Taizong's younger brother, so Chucai spoke to Ruizong, saying, "This is a great matter of altars and state; it should be settled early."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong was then Taizong's younger brother, so Chucai told him, "This is a matter of altars and state and should be settled at once."

sentences.zh: 睿宗曰：「事猶未集，別擇日可乎？」

translations.literal: Ruizong said, "The matter is not yet ready—might we choose another day?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong said, "The arrangements are not complete—could we choose another day?"

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「過是無吉日矣。」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "After this there will be no auspicious day."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "After that there will be no auspicious day left."

sentences.zh: 遂定策，立儀制，乃告親王察合台曰：「王雖兄，位則臣也，禮當拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon the plan was fixed and ceremonial regulations established; he then told Prince Chagatai, "Though you are the elder brother, in rank you are a subject; by ritual you should bow.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was fixed and court ceremony established; he then told Prince Chagatai, "Though you are the elder brother, in rank you are a subject and should bow by ritual.

sentences.zh: 王拜，則莫敢不拜。」

translations.literal: When you bow, none will dare not bow."
translations.idiomatic: If you bow, none will dare refuse."

sentences.zh: 王深然之。

translations.literal: The prince deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The prince strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及即位，王率皇族及臣僚拜帳下，既退，王撫楚材曰：「真社稷臣也。」

translations.literal: When the enthronement took place, the prince led the imperial clan and officials in bowing before the tent; after they withdrew, the prince patted Chucai and said, "A true minister of altars and state."
translations.idiomatic: At the enthronement the prince led the imperial clan and officials in bowing before the tent; afterward he patted Chucai and said, "A true minister of the realm."

sentences.zh: 國朝尊屬有拜禮自此始。

translations.literal: From this the dynasty's custom of bowing by honored kinsmen began.
translations.idiomatic: From this the dynasty's custom of bowing by senior imperial kinsmen began.

sentences.zh: 時朝集後期應死者眾，楚材奏曰：「陛下新即位，宜宥之。」

translations.literal: At the time many who were late for court assembly should have been put to death; Chucai memorialized, "Your Majesty has newly ascended; they should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Many who were late for court assembly were due for execution; Chucai memorialized, "Your Majesty has just ascended—they should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 太宗從之。

translations.literal: Taizong followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 中原甫定，民多誤觸禁網，而國法無赦令。

translations.literal: The Central Plains had just been pacified; many among the people inadvertently touched the prohibitions of the law, while the national code had no amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains had only just been pacified; many people had unwittingly broken the law, yet the state code provided no amnesty.

sentences.zh: 楚材議請肆宥，眾以為迂，楚材獨從容為帝言。

translations.literal: Chucai proposed requesting a general pardon; the multitude thought this impractical, but Chucai alone calmly spoke to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai urged a general pardon; most thought the idea impractical, but he alone spoke calmly to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔自庚寅正月朔日前事勿治。

translations.literal: An edict declared that matters before the first day of the first month of the year gengyin were not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that offenses committed before the New Year of the gengyin year would not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 且條便宜一十八事頒天下，其略言：「郡宜置長吏牧民，設萬戶總軍，使勢均力敵，以遏驕橫。

translations.literal: Moreover he set forth eighteen expedient measures to be promulgated throughout the realm, in summary saying: "Each commandery should appoint a chief official to shepherd the people and establish ten-thousand-household chiefs to command the army, so that power and strength are evenly matched and arrogance is checked.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted eighteen administrative measures for promulgation nationwide, in brief: "Each commandery should have a civil magistrate to govern the people and a ten-thousand-household chief to command troops, their powers balanced so that arrogance may be checked.

sentences.zh: 中原之地，財用所出，宜存卹其民，州縣非奉上命，敢擅行科差者罪之。

translations.literal: The lands of the Central Plains are the source of wealth and supplies; the people should be preserved and comforted; if prefectures and districts, without receiving orders from above, dare on their own to impose levies and corvée, they are to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains are the treasury of the realm; their people must be protected. Any prefecture or district that levies taxes or corvée without imperial authority is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 貿易借貸官物者罪之。

translations.literal: Those who trade in or borrow and lend government goods are to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Trading in or lending out government property is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、回鶻、河西諸人，種地不納稅者死。

translations.literal: Mongols, Uighurs, and people of Hexi who cultivate land but do not pay taxes are to die.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols, Uighurs, and people of Hexi who farm land but refuse to pay taxes are to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 監主自盜官物者死。

translations.literal: Supervisors who themselves steal government goods are to die.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors who embezzle government goods are to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 應犯死罪者，具由申奏待報，然後行刑。

translations.literal: Those who should be guilty of capital crimes must set forth the grounds, memorialize and await report, and only then carry out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases must be reported in full to the throne and await approval before execution.

sentences.zh: 貢獻禮物，為害非輕，深宜禁斷。」

translations.literal: Presenting tribute and gifts does harm that is no small matter; it should be deeply forbidden and cut off."
translations.idiomatic: The presenting of tribute gifts does grave harm and ought to be strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之，唯貢獻一事不允，曰：「彼自願饋獻者，宜聽之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all of this, save only the matter of tribute gifts, which he did not approve, saying, "If they of their own will wish to present gifts, they should be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of this except the ban on tribute gifts, saying, "If people wish to offer gifts of their own accord, they should be allowed."

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「蠹害之端，必由於此。」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The beginning of corruption must come from this."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Corruption always begins here."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「凡卿所奏，無不從者，卿不能從朕一事耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "In all that you memorialize there is nothing I do not follow—can you not follow me in this one matter?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have never refused a single proposal of yours—can you not yield to me on this one point?"

sentences.zh: 太祖之世，歲有事西域，未暇經理中原，官吏多聚斂自私，貲至巨萬，而官無儲彳侍。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time, year after year there were campaigns in the Western Regions and no leisure to administer the Central Plains; officials mostly amassed wealth for themselves, their assets reaching tens of thousands, while the government had no reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Taizu's reign campaigns in the west left no time to govern the Central Plains; officials enriched themselves by the tens of thousands while the treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 近臣別迭等言：「漢人無補於國，可悉空其人以為牧地。」

translations.literal: The close attendant Biedie and others said, "Han people are of no benefit to the state; we can entirely clear them out and make the land pasture."
translations.idiomatic: The intimate adviser Biedie and others said, "The Han are useless to the state; drive them all out and turn the land into pasture."

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「陛下將南伐，軍需宜有所資，誠均定中原地稅、商稅、鹽、酒、鐵冶、山澤之利，歲可得銀五十萬兩、帛八萬匹、粟四十餘萬石，足以供給，何謂無補哉？」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "Your Majesty is about to campaign south; military supplies ought to have some source of support; if we truly fix and assess land tax, commercial tax, and the profits of salt, wine, iron smelting, and mountain and marsh resources in the Central Plains, each year we can obtain five hundred thousand taels of silver, eighty thousand bolts of silk, and more than four hundred thousand piculs of grain—enough to supply needs—how can you say they are of no benefit?"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai replied, "Your Majesty is about to march south; the army must be fed. If we levy land tax, commercial tax, and revenues from salt, wine, iron, and natural resources across the Central Plains, we can raise five hundred thousand taels of silver, eighty thousand bolts of silk, and more than four hundred thousand piculs of grain a year—enough for any campaign. How can the Han be called useless?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿試為朕行之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You try it for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then put your plan into practice for me."

sentences.zh: 乃奏立燕京等十路徵收課稅使，凡長貳悉用士人，如陳時可、趙昉等，皆寬厚長者，極天下之選，參佐皆用省部舊人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized to establish tax-collection commissioners for the ten circuits including Yanjing; all chief and deputy posts were filled with scholar-officials such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang, all men of generous and mature character, the finest selection in the realm, and assistants were all drawn from former personnel of the provincial departments.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to establish tax commissioners for the ten circuits including Yanjing, appointing cultivated men such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang—men of the finest character in the realm—with assistants drawn from former central-government staff.

sentences.zh: 辛卯秋，帝至雲中，十路咸進廩籍及金帛陳於廷中，帝笑謂楚材曰：「汝不去朕左右，而能使國用充足，南國之臣，復有如卿者乎？

translations.literal: In autumn of the year xinmao the Emperor reached Yunzhong; all ten circuits presented granary registers and gold and silk displayed in the court; the Emperor smiled and said to Chucai, "You do not leave my side, yet can make state revenues ample—among the ministers of the southern states, is there again one like you?
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the xinmao year the emperor reached Yunzhong; all ten circuits presented their granary registers and tribute of gold and silk in court. Smiling, the emperor said to Chucai, "You never leave my side, yet you fill the treasury—is there another minister in the southern lands like you?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「在彼者皆賢於臣，臣不才，故留燕，為陛下用。」

translations.literal: " He replied, "Those there are all more worthy than I; I am without talent, and therefore remained in Yan to be used by Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "The men there are all more capable than I; I lack talent, which is why I stayed in Yan to serve Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其謙，賜之酒。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his modesty and bestowed wine on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his modesty and rewarded him with wine.

sentences.zh: 即日拜中書令，事無鉅細，皆先白之。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Director of the Secretariat; in affairs great and small all were first reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed director of the Secretariat; thereafter every matter, great or small, was referred to him first.

sentences.zh: 楚材奏：「凡州郡宜令長吏專理民事，萬戶總軍政，凡所掌課稅，權貴不得侵之。」

translations.literal: Chucai memorialized: "In every prefecture and district the chief official should be ordered to administer civil affairs exclusively, and the ten-thousand-household chief to command military affairs; all tax revenues under their charge the powerful must not encroach upon."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai memorialized: "In every prefecture the civil magistrate should handle civil affairs alone and the ten-thousand-household chief military affairs alone, and no powerful figure may seize the taxes under their charge."

sentences.zh: 又舉鎮海、粘合，均與之同事，權貴不能平。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zhenhai and Nianhe to share office with him equally; the powerful could not be reconciled to this.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Zhenhai and Nianhe to serve alongside him, which the powerful resented.

sentences.zh: 咸得卜以舊怨，尤疾之，譖於宗王曰：「耶律中書令率用親舊，必有二心，宜奏殺之。」

translations.literal: Xiandebo, because of an old grudge, especially hated him and slandered him to a prince of the blood, saying, "The Yelü Director of the Secretariat chiefly employs kin and old associates; he must have a divided heart—he should be memorialized for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Xiandebo, nursing an old grudge, hated him all the more and slandered him to a imperial prince: "The Yelü director of the Secretariat fills his office with kin and cronies; he must be disloyal—memorialize for his execution."

sentences.zh: 宗王遣使以聞，帝察其誣，責使者，罷遣之。

translations.literal: The prince sent an envoy to report; the Emperor perceived the falsehood, reproved the envoy, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent an envoy to report this; the emperor saw through the slander, rebuked the envoy, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 屬有訟咸得卜不法者，帝命楚材鞫之，奏曰：「此人倨傲，故易招謗。

translations.literal: When there came a suit against Xiandebo for unlawful conduct, the Emperor ordered Chucai to try him; he memorialized, "This man is arrogant, and therefore easily invites slander.
translations.idiomatic: When a lawsuit was brought against Xiandebo for misconduct, the emperor ordered Chucai to try him; Chucai reported, "This man is arrogant and therefore invites slander.

sentences.zh: 今將有事南方，他日治之未晚也。」

translations.literal: We are about to have business in the south; to deal with him another day will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: We are about to campaign in the south; there will be time enough to deal with him afterward."

sentences.zh: 帝私謂侍臣曰：「楚材不較私仇，真寬厚長者，汝曹當效之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor privately told his attendants, "Chucai does not settle private scores—truly a generous and mature man; you should emulate him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants privately, "Chucai will not settle private scores—a truly generous man; you should take him as your model."

sentences.zh: 中貴可思不花奏採金銀役夫及種田西域與栽蒲萄戶，帝令於西京宣德徙萬餘戶充之。

translations.literal: The palace favorite Kesibuhua memorialized to recruit laborers for mining gold and silver and households to farm in the Western Regions and plant grapes; the Emperor ordered that more than ten thousand households be moved from Xijing and Xuande to fill these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The palace favorite Kesibuhua proposed drafting laborers to mine gold and silver and households to farm in the Western Regions and plant vineyards; the emperor ordered more than ten thousand households moved from Xijing and Xuande to fill the quotas.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「先帝遺詔，山後民質樸，無異國人，緩急可用，不宜輕動。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The late Emperor's testamentary edict said that the people behind the mountains are simple and honest, no different from our own people, and in urgency or ease can be used—they should not be lightly moved.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The late emperor's testament declared that the people north of the mountains are plain and loyal, no different from our own folk, and useful in crisis—they should not be uprooted lightly.

sentences.zh: 今將徵河南，請無殘民以給此役。」

translations.literal: We are now about to campaign in Henan; I request that the people not be ravaged to supply this labor service."
translations.idiomatic: We are about to campaign in Henan; I beg that the people not be ravaged to supply this labor."

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 壬辰春，帝南征，將涉河，詔逃難之民，來降者免死。

translations.literal: In spring of the year renchen the Emperor campaigned south; about to cross the river, he decreed that refugees who came to surrender would be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the renchen year the emperor marched south; as he was about to cross the river, he decreed that refugees who surrendered would be spared.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此輩急則降，緩則走，徒以資敵，不可宥。」

translations.literal: Some said, "These people when pressed surrender, when eased flee—they only supply the enemy and cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued, "They surrender when pressed and flee when the pressure eases—they only strengthen the enemy and must not be spared."

sentences.zh: 楚材請制旗數百，以給降民，使歸田裡，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Chucai requested that several hundred banners be made and given to the surrendered people, enabling them to return to their villages and fields; very many were thereby preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai asked that several hundred banners be made for the surrendered people so they could return to their fields; a great multitude were thus saved.

sentences.zh: 舊制，凡攻城邑，敵以矢石相加者，即為拒命，既克，必殺之。

translations.literal: By old regulation, whenever a walled city was attacked, if the enemy exchanged arrows and stones, that counted as defiance; once taken, they were invariably killed.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, any city that resisted with arrows and stones was deemed defiant and, once taken, its people were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 汴梁將下，大將速不台遣使來言：「金人抗拒持久，師多死傷，城下之日，宜屠之。」

translations.literal: When Bianliang was about to fall, the great general Subutai sent a messenger saying, "The Jin resisted for a long time; many in the army were killed or wounded; on the day the city is taken, it should be put to the sword."
translations.idiomatic: As Bianliang was about to fall, the general Subutai sent word: "The Jin resisted for so long that our army suffered heavy losses; when the city falls, it should be slaughtered."

sentences.zh: 楚材馳入奏曰：「將士暴露數十年，所欲者土地人民耳。

translations.literal: Chucai galloped in to memorialize, "The officers and soldiers have been exposed to wind and weather for decades; what they desire is land and people.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai rode in at once and said, "Our soldiers have campaigned in the open for decades; what they want is land and people.

sentences.zh: 得地無民，將焉用之！」

translations.literal: To gain land without people—how will it be used!"
translations.idiomatic: What use is land without people?"

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫未決，楚材曰：「奇巧之工，厚藏之家，皆萃於此，若盡殺之，將無所獲。」

translations.literal: The Emperor hesitated and had not decided; Chucai said, "Skilled artisans of rare craft and families of deep wealth are all gathered here; if we kill them all, we will gain nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hesitated; Chucai said, "The finest craftsmen and the wealthiest households are all in this city; if we kill them all, we shall gain nothing."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，詔罪止完顏氏，餘皆勿問。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed; an edict declared that guilt rested only on the Wanyan clan, and the rest were not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and decreed that only the Wanyan clan would be held guilty; all others were to go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 時避兵居汴者得百四十七萬人。

translations.literal: At the time those who had taken refuge from war in Bian numbered one million four hundred seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had taken refuge from the fighting in Bian numbered one million four hundred and seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 楚材又請遣人入城，求孔子後，得五十一代孫元措，奏襲封衍聖公，付以林廟地。

translations.literal: Chucai again requested that men be sent into the city to seek a descendant of Confucius; they obtained Yuan Cuo, fifty-first-generation descendant, memorialized to confer on him the inherited title Duke Yansheng, and entrusted to him the forest and temple lands.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai also asked that men be sent into the city to find a descendant of Confucius; they found Yuan Cuo, fifty-first in line, and memorialized that he inherit the title Duke Yansheng with charge of the temple estates.

sentences.zh: 命收太常禮樂生，及召名儒梁陟、王萬慶、趙著等，使直釋九經，進講東宮。

translations.literal: He ordered the collection of ritual and music students of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and summoned eminent Confucians Liang Zhi, Wang Wanqing, Zhao Zhu, and others, making them attend to the exegesis of the Nine Classics and lecture in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the recruitment of ritual musicians from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and summoned eminent scholars Liang Zhi, Wang Wanqing, Zhao Zhu, and others to annotate the Nine Classics and lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 又率大臣子孫，執經解義，俾知聖人之道。

translations.literal: He also led the sons and grandsons of great ministers to hold the classics and explain their meaning, so that they might know the Way of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered the sons and grandsons of high ministers to study the classics and their commentaries, so that they might learn the Way of the sages.

sentences.zh: 置編修所於燕京、經籍所於平陽，由是文治興焉。

translations.literal: He established a Compilation Office at Yanjing and a Classics Office at Pingyang; thereby civil governance flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He established a compilation office at Yanjing and a classics office at Pingyang, and from this literary government began to flourish.

sentences.zh: 時河南初破，俘獲甚眾，軍還，逃者十七八。

translations.literal: At the time Henan had just been taken; captives were very numerous; when the army returned, seven or eight in ten had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had just been conquered and captives were many, but when the army withdrew seven or eight in ten had escaped.

sentences.zh: 有旨：居停逃民及資給者，滅其家，鄉社亦連坐。

translations.literal: There was an order: those who harbored fugitive people or supplied them were to have their families exterminated, and village communities were also to be punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out that anyone who harbored or aided fugitives would have his household destroyed and his community punished as well.

sentences.zh: 由是逃者莫敢舍，多殍死道路。

translations.literal: Because of this the fugitives dared take shelter nowhere, and many starved to death on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives dared seek shelter nowhere, and many starved to death along the roads.

sentences.zh: 楚材從容進曰：「河南既平，民皆陛下赤子，走復何之！

translations.literal: Chucai calmly advanced and said, "Henan is already pacified; the people are all Your Majesty's children—where would they flee!
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said calmly, "Henan is already pacified; these people are all your children—where can they flee?

sentences.zh: 奈何因一俘囚，連死數十百人乎？」

translations.literal: How can we, because of one captive, cause the linked death of dozens or hundreds of people?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should dozens or hundreds die because of a single fugitive?"

sentences.zh: 帝悟，命除其禁。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and ordered the prohibition removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and ordered the prohibition lifted.

sentences.zh: 金之亡也，唯秦、鞏二十餘州久未下，楚材奏曰：「往年吾民逃罪，或萃於此，故以死拒戰，若許以不殺，將不攻自下矣。」

translations.literal: In the fall of Jin, only more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gong had long not submitted; Chucai memorialized, "In former years our people fled crimes and some gathered here; therefore they fight to the death in resistance; if we promise not to kill, they will submit without attack."
translations.idiomatic: As Jin was collapsing, more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gong still held out; Chucai memorialized, "In past years fugitives from our rule gathered there and now fight to the death; promise them their lives and they will surrender without a siege."

sentences.zh: 詔下，諸城皆降。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, all the cities surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, every city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 甲午，議籍中原民，大臣忽都虎等議，以丁為戶。

translations.literal: In the year jiawu they deliberated on registering the people of the Central Plains; the great minister Huduqu and others proposed taking adult males as the household unit.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year they debated registering the people of the Central Plains; the minister Huduqu and others proposed counting adult males as households.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 丁逃，則賦無所出，當以戶定之。」

translations.literal: If adult males flee, then there is nowhere for levies to come from; households should be the unit of assessment."
translations.idiomatic: If adult males flee, revenue has nowhere to come from; registration should be by household."

sentences.zh: 爭之再三，卒以戶定。

translations.literal: He argued back and forth repeatedly, and in the end household registration was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the point again and again until household registration was finally adopted.

sentences.zh: 時將相大臣有所驅獲，往往寄留諸郡，楚材因括戶口，並令為民，匿佔者死。

translations.literal: At the time generals, ministers, and great officials who had seized people often left them registered in various commanderies; Chucai therefore conducted a household census, ordered them all to be made common subjects, and those who concealed or seized them were to die.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and ministers often left captives registered in distant commanderies; Chucai conducted a census, declared them common subjects, and made concealment or seizure a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 乙未，朝議將四征不廷，若遣回回人徵江南，漢人征西域，深得制御之術，楚材曰：「不可。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei the court deliberated on the four campaigns of those who had not attended court; some proposed that if Huihui men were sent to conquer Jiangnan and Han men to conquer the Western Regions, this would deeply grasp the art of control; Chucai said, "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year the court debated campaigns against absent princes; some argued that sending Muslims to conquer Jiangnan and Han Chinese to the Western Regions would be masterful control; Chucai said, "That will not work.

sentences.zh: 中原、西域，相去遼遠，未至敵境，人馬疲乏，兼水土異宜，疾疫將生，宜各從其便。」

translations.literal: The Central Plains and the Western Regions are vastly distant from each other; before reaching enemy territory men and horses are exhausted, and moreover water and soil differ in suitability—epidemics will arise; each should follow what is convenient to them."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains and the Western Regions are far apart; troops would be exhausted before they reached the enemy, and unfamiliar climates would breed epidemics. Each region should fight with its own people."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙申春，諸王大集，帝親執觴賜楚材曰：「朕之所以推誠任卿者，先帝之命也。

translations.literal: In spring of the year bingshen the princes gathered in great numbers; the Emperor personally held a cup and bestowed it on Chucai, saying, "The reason I trust you with full sincerity is the late Emperor's command.
translations.idiomatic: That spring in the bingshen year, when the princes assembled, the emperor personally raised a cup to Chucai and said, "I place my full trust in you because the late emperor commanded it.

sentences.zh: 非卿，則中原無今日。

translations.literal: Without you, the Central Plains would not have today.
translations.idiomatic: Without you the Central Plains would not be what they are today.

sentences.zh: 朕所以得安枕者，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: That I can sleep at ease is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: It is through your efforts that I can sleep in peace."

sentences.zh: 西域諸國及宋、高麗使者來朝，語多不實，帝指楚材示之曰：「汝國有如此人乎？」

translations.literal: Envoys from the states of the Western Regions and from Song and Goryeo came to court; their words were mostly untrue; the Emperor pointed to Chucai and showed him to them, saying, "Does your state have a man like this?"
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from the Western Regions, Song, and Goryeo came to court with their usual exaggerations, the emperor pointed to Chucai and asked, "Does your country have anyone like him?"

sentences.zh: 皆謝曰：「無有。

translations.literal: All apologized and said, "There is not.
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "No, there is not.

sentences.zh: 殆神人也。」

translations.literal: He is almost a divine man."
translations.idiomatic: He is scarcely human."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝等唯此言不妄，朕亦度必無此人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "In this alone your words are not false; I too reckon that there surely is no such person."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That alone you do not lie about; I too am sure no such man exists anywhere."

sentences.zh: 有於元者，奏行交鈔，楚材曰：「金章宗時初行交鈔，與錢通行，有司以出鈔為利，收鈔為諱，謂之老鈔，至以萬貫唯易一餅。

translations.literal: Someone at court memorialized to issue paper notes; Chucai said, "When Jin Emperor Zhangzong first issued paper notes, they circulated with coin; the offices took issuing notes as profit and collecting notes as taboo, calling them old notes, until ten thousand strings could buy only one cake.
translations.idiomatic: Someone at court proposed issuing paper currency; Chucai said, "When Jin Emperor Zhangzong first issued paper notes, they circulated alongside coin, but officials profited by printing and shunned redeeming—'old notes' until ten thousand strings bought a single cake.

sentences.zh: 民力困竭，國用匱乏，當為鑑戒。

translations.literal: The people's strength was exhausted and state revenues depleted—this should serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted and the treasury empty—that should be our warning.

sentences.zh: 今印造交鈔，宜不過萬錠。」

translations.literal: Now in printing paper notes, it should not exceed ten thousand ingots."
translations.idiomatic: If we print notes now, the issue should not exceed ten thousand ingots."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，忽都虎以民籍至，帝議裂州縣賜親王功臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Huduqu arrived with the household registers; the Emperor deliberated on carving up prefectures and districts to bestow on imperial princes and meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Huduqu delivered the household registers, and the emperor considered dividing prefectures among princes and meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「裂土分民，易生嫌隙，不如多以金帛與之。」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "To split land and divide the people easily breeds suspicion and rifts; it would be better to give them more gold and silk."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Dividing land and people breeds suspicion; better to reward them generously with gold and silk."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已許奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "It has already been promised—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already promised—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「若朝廷置吏，收其貢賦，歲終頒之，使毋擅科徵，可也。」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "If the court appoints officials, collects their tribute and levies, and at year's end distributes them, so that they may not levy on their own authority, that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Let the court appoint officials to collect tribute and distribute it at year's end, forbidding private levies—that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 帝然其計，遂定天下賦稅，每二戶出絲一斤，以給國用；

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his plan and thereupon fixed the realm's taxes: every two households were to contribute one jin of silk for state use;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and fixed the realm's taxes: every two households owed one jin of silk for state revenue;

sentences.zh: 五戶出絲一斤，以給諸王功臣湯沐之資。

translations.literal: five households one jin of silk, to supply the bathing-fief funds of the princes and meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: and every five households one jin for the princes' and ministers' maintenance allotments.

sentences.zh: 地稅，中田每畝二升又半，上田三升，下田二升，水田每畝五升；

translations.literal: Land tax: on middling fields two and a half sheng per mu, on upper fields three sheng, on lower fields two sheng, on paddy fields five sheng per mu;
translations.idiomatic: Land tax was set at two and a half sheng per mu for middling fields, three for upper fields, two for lower fields, and five for paddy;

sentences.zh: 商稅，三十分而一；

translations.literal: commercial tax, one part in thirty;
translations.idiomatic: commercial tax at one-thirtieth;

sentences.zh: 鹽價，銀一兩四十斤。

translations.literal: salt price, one tael of silver for forty jin.
translations.idiomatic: and salt at forty jin per tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 既定常賦，朝議以為太輕，楚材曰：「作法於涼，其弊猶貪，後將有以利進者，則今已重矣。」

translations.literal: Once the regular levies were fixed, the court considered them too light; Chucai said, "If one makes law in cool times, its abuse is still greed; later there will be those who advance by profit—then what is light today will already be heavy."
translations.idiomatic: When the regular levies were fixed, the court thought them too light; Chucai said, "Even lenient laws breed greed; once men advance by squeezing profit from the people, today's light burden will seem heavy enough."

sentences.zh: 時工匠製造，糜費官物，十私八九，楚材請皆考核之，以為定制。

translations.literal: At the time artisans in manufacture squandered government goods, eight or nine in ten for private use; Chucai requested that all be audited and made a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans were wasting government materials, keeping eight or nine parts in ten for themselves; Chucai ordered audits and fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 時侍臣脫歡奏簡天下室女，詔下，楚材尼之不行，帝怒。

translations.literal: At the time the attendant Toqan memorialized to select maidens throughout the realm; when the edict was issued Chucai blocked it from being carried out, and the Emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant Toqan proposed selecting maidens empire-wide; when the edict was issued Chucai blocked its execution, and the emperor grew angry.

sentences.zh: 楚材進曰：「向擇美女二十有八人，足備使令。

translations.literal: Chucai advanced and said, "Previously twenty-eight beautiful women were chosen—enough to serve at command.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Twenty-eight women have already been chosen—enough for the palace.

sentences.zh: 今復選拔，臣恐擾民，欲覆奏耳。」

translations.literal: To select again now—I fear disturbing the people and wished only to memorialize again."
translations.idiomatic: Another selection would distress the people; I only wished to report back to you."

sentences.zh: 帝良久曰：「可罷之。」

translations.literal: After a long while the Emperor said, "It may be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor said, "Let it be canceled."

sentences.zh: 又欲收民牝馬，楚材曰：「田蠶之地，非馬所產，今若行之，後必為人害。」

translations.literal: He also wished to collect the people's brood mares; Chucai said, "In lands of fields and silkworms horses are not produced; if this is done now, later it will surely harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wanted to seize the people's brood mares; Chucai said, "These are farming and silk country, not horse country; do this now and it will harm the people for years to come."

sentences.zh: 又從之。

translations.literal: Again this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，楚材奏曰：「制器者必用良工，守成者必用儒臣。

translations.literal: In the year dingyou Chucai memorialized, "Those who make vessels must use skilled artisans; those who preserve an inheritance must use Confucian ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year Chucai memorialized, "Making vessels requires skilled craftsmen; preserving a realm requires Confucian ministers.

sentences.zh: 儒臣之事業，非積數十年，殆未易成也。」

translations.literal: The enterprise of Confucian ministers is not accumulated over mere decades—it is scarcely easy to accomplish."
translations.idiomatic: Their craft is not mastered in a few decades—it is hard won."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「果爾，可官其人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If it is truly so, their persons may be given office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If that is so, then give them office."

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「請校試之。」

translations.literal: Chucai said, "I request that they be examined and tested."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Let them be examined first."

sentences.zh: 乃命宣德州宣課使劉中隨郡考試，以經義、詞賦、論分為三科，儒人被俘為奴者，亦令就試，其主匿弗遣者死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuanede Prefecture, to conduct examinations in each commandery, divided into three categories—classics, rhapsodies, and discourses; Confucian scholars taken captive as slaves were also ordered to sit the examination, and masters who concealed them and did not send them were to die.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuanede, to hold examinations in every commandery in three fields—classics, rhapsodies, and policy essays. Captured scholars enslaved were also to sit the exam; masters who hid them were put to death.

sentences.zh: 得士凡四千三十人，免為奴者四之一。

translations.literal: Scholars obtained numbered four thousand thirty in all; one in four were freed from slavery.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand and thirty scholars passed; one in four were freed from slavery.

sentences.zh: 先是，州郡長吏，多藉賈人銀以償官，息累數倍，曰羊羔兒利，至奴其妻子猶不足償。

translations.literal: Earlier, prefectural and district chiefs mostly borrowed merchants' silver to repay the government; interest accumulated several times over, called "lamb-kid interest," until even enslaving their wives and children was insufficient to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Previously local magistrates often borrowed silver from merchants to meet government quotas at usurious "lamb-kid" rates, until even selling their wives and children could not repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 楚材奏令本利相侔而止，永為定制，民間所負者，官為代價之。

translations.literal: Chucai memorialized that principal and interest should be made equal and then stop, permanently as a fixed regulation, and what the people owed the government would repay on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai memorialized that interest should not exceed principal and that the state would redeem private debts—a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 至一衡量，給符印，立鈔法，定均輸，布遞傳，明驛券，庶政略備，民稍蘇息焉。

translations.literal: He unified weights and measures, issued tallies and seals, established paper-note law, fixed equalized transport, deployed relay posts, clarified post warrants—in general administration was largely complete, and the people were somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: He standardized weights and measures, issued seals and tallies, established paper currency, fixed transport quotas, organized courier routes, and clarified post warrants; civil administration was largely in place, and the people began to recover.

sentences.zh: 有二道士爭長，互立黨與，其一誣其仇之黨二人為逃軍，結中貴及通事楊惟忠，執而虐殺之。

translations.literal: Two Daoist priests contended for seniority and each formed factions; one falsely accused two men of his enemy's faction as deserters, joined with a palace favorite and the interpreter Yang Weizhong, seized them, and cruelly killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Two Daoist priests vied for precedence and formed factions; one framed two men from the rival faction as deserters, enlisted a palace favorite and the interpreter Yang Weizhong, seized them, and tortured them to death.

sentences.zh: 楚材按收惟忠。

translations.literal: Chucai investigated and arrested Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai investigated and arrested Weizhong.

sentences.zh: 中貴复訴楚材違制，帝怒，系楚材；

translations.literal: The palace favorite again accused Chucai of violating regulations; the Emperor was angry and imprisoned Chucai;
translations.idiomatic: The palace favorite accused Chucai of overstepping his authority; the emperor was furious and had Chucai bound;

sentences.zh: 既而自悔，命釋之。

translations.literal: then repented and ordered him released.
translations.idiomatic: then repented and ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 楚材不肯解縛，進曰：「臣備位公輔，國政所屬。

translations.literal: Chucai would not accept being unbound and advanced, saying, "I occupy the position of chief minister; state affairs are my charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai refused to be unbound and said, "I hold the highest office; the governance of the realm is my charge.

sentences.zh: 陛下初令系臣，以有罪也，當明示百官，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ordered me bound, it was because I had guilt and should have been clearly shown to the hundred officials as guilty of unpardonable crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first had me bound, it was because I was guilty and should have been shown to the officials as deserving death.

sentences.zh: 今釋臣，是無罪也，豈宜輕易反覆，如戲小兒？

translations.literal: Now to release me is to say I am without guilt—how can one lightly turn back and forth as if playing with a child?
translations.idiomatic: To release me now is to declare me innocent—how can the throne turn about as if playing with a child?

sentences.zh: 國有大事，何以行焉！」

translations.literal: When the state has great affairs, how can they be carried out!"
translations.idiomatic: How can great affairs of state be conducted in this way!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆失色。

translations.literal: The assembly all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the hall turned pale.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕雖為帝，寧無過舉耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Though I am emperor, can I be without mistaken actions?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even an emperor can err, can he not?"

sentences.zh: 乃溫言以慰之。

translations.literal: Thereupon with gentle words he comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to him gently and consoled him.

sentences.zh: 楚材因陳時務十策，曰：「信賞罰，正名分，給俸祿，官功臣，考殿最，均科差，選工匠，務農桑，定土貢，制漕運。」

translations.literal: Chucai thereupon presented ten policies on current affairs, saying: "Trust in rewards and punishments, rectify names and ranks, grant salaries, appoint meritorious ministers, examine best and worst performance, equalize levies and corvée, select artisans, devote effort to farming and sericulture, fix local tribute, and regulate grain transport by water."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai then presented ten policies for the times: "Enforce rewards and punishments, rectify ranks and titles, pay salaries, appoint meritorious men, grade official performance, equalize levies, select artisans, promote farming and sericulture, fix local tribute, and regulate grain transport."

sentences.zh: 皆切於時務，悉施行之。

translations.literal: All were urgent to current affairs and were fully put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: All were urgently relevant, and all were put into practice.

sentences.zh: 太原路轉運使呂振、副使劉子振，以贓抵罪。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, transport commissioner of Taiyuan Circuit, and Vice Commissioner Liu Zizhen were punished for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, transport commissioner of Taiyuan Circuit, and his deputy Liu Zizhen were convicted of corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝責楚材曰：「卿言孔子之教可行，儒者為好人，何故乃有此輩？」

translations.literal: The Emperor reproached Chucai, saying, "You said Confucius's teaching can be practiced and that Confucians are good men—why then are there men like these?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Chucai: "You said Confucian teaching could govern the realm and that scholars were good men—why then do we have men like these?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「君父教臣子，亦不欲令陷不義。

translations.literal: He replied, "A lord and father in teaching his ministers and sons also does not wish to make them fall into unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Even a father teaching his sons does not wish them to fall into wickedness.

sentences.zh: 三綱五常，聖人之名教，有國家者莫不由之，如天之有日月也。

translations.literal: The Three Bonds and Five Constants are the sages' teaching by name; those who have states all follow them, as Heaven has sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Bonds and Five Constants are the sages' teaching; every state lives by them as Heaven has sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 豈得緣一夫之失，使萬世常行之道獨見廢於我朝乎！」

translations.literal: How can we, because of one man's fault, let the Way constantly practiced for ten thousand generations alone be abandoned in our dynasty!"
translations.idiomatic: Can one man's failure justify abandoning in our dynasty the Way that has governed all ages!"

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 富人劉忽篤馬、涉獵發丁、劉廷玉等以銀一百四十萬兩撲買天下課稅，楚材曰：「此貪利之徒，罔上虐下，為害甚大。」

translations.literal: The rich men Liu Huduma, Shelie Fading, Liu Tingyu, and others with 1,400,000 taels of silver bid to monopolize purchase of the realm's tax revenues; Chucai said, "These are men greedy for profit who deceive superiors and abuse inferiors—the harm is very great."
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy Liu Huduma, Shelie Fading, Liu Tingyu, and others offered 1,400,000 taels to monopolize the empire's tax revenues; Chucai said, "These profiteers deceive the throne and oppress the people—the harm is immense."

sentences.zh: 奏罷之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and had the scheme abolished.

sentences.zh: 常曰： 「興一利不如除一害，生一事不如省一事。

translations.literal: He often said: "To create one benefit is not as good as removing one harm; to generate one affair is not as good as eliminating one affair.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Better to remove one harm than to create one benefit; better to cut one burden than to add one task.

sentences.zh: 任尚以班超之言為平平耳，千古之下，自有定論。

translations.literal: Ren Shang took Ban Chao's words as merely ordinary; after a thousand ages there will naturally be a settled judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shang thought Ban Chao's words commonplace, but posterity will judge otherwise.

sentences.zh: 後之負譴者，方知吾言之不妄也。」

translations.literal: Those later who bear reproof will then know that my words were not false."
translations.idiomatic: Those who come after and bear blame will know I spoke no falsehood."

sentences.zh: 帝素嗜酒，日與大臣酣飲，楚材屢諫，不聽，乃持酒槽鐵口進曰：「曲蘗能腐物，鐵尚如此，況五臟乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor had always loved wine and daily drank deeply with his ministers; Chucai repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded; he then took a wine trough with an iron mouth and advanced, saying, "Yeast lees can rot things—if iron is thus, how much more the five viscera!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved wine and drank daily with his ministers; Chucai remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then brought a wine trough with an iron spout and said, "Ferment can rot iron—what will it do to the five organs!"

sentences.zh: 帝悟，語近臣曰： 「汝曹愛君憂國之心，豈有如吾圖撒合裡者耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and told his close ministers, "In the heart of loving the ruler and worrying for the state, is there anyone like our Uqtu Saqal?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and told his intimates, "Who among you loves the ruler and cares for the state as Uqtu Saqal does?"

sentences.zh: 賞以金帛，敕近臣日進酒三鐘而止。

translations.literal: He rewarded him with gold and silk and charged the close ministers that daily wine presented should stop at three cups.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with gold and silk and ordered his intimates to limit the emperor to three cups a day.

sentences.zh: 自庚寅定課稅格，至甲午平河南，歲有增羨，至戊戌，課銀增至一百一十萬兩。

translations.literal: From fixing the tax scale in gengyin to pacifying Henan in jiawu, each year there was increase; by wuxu tax silver had risen to 1,100,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: From the gengyin year when the tax scale was fixed until Henan was pacified in the jiawu year, revenues rose yearly; by the wuxu year tax silver reached 1,100,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 譯史安天合者，諂事鎮海，首引奧都剌合蠻撲買課稅，又增至二百二十萬兩。

translations.literal: The interpreter An Tianhe, who flattered Zhenhai, first introduced Oqturqalmish to bid to monopolize tax revenues, raising them again to 2,200,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreter An Tianhe, who curried favor with Zhenhai, introduced Oqturqalmish's bid to monopolize tax collection, raising the quota to 2,200,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 楚材極力辨諫，至聲色俱厲，言與涕俱。

translations.literal: Chucai argued and remonstrated with all his strength, until voice and countenance were both severe, words and tears together.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai argued with all his strength until his voice shook and tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾欲搏鬥耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Do you wish to wrestle?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you want to fight me?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「爾欲為百姓哭耶？

translations.literal: He also said, "Do you wish to weep for the common people?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Do you want to weep for the people?

sentences.zh: 姑令試行之。」

translations.literal: For the moment let it be tried."
translations.idiomatic: Let it be tried for now."

sentences.zh: 楚材力不能止，乃嘆息曰：「民之困窮，將自此始矣！」

translations.literal: Chucai could not stop it by force and sighed, saying, "The people's distress and poverty will begin from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Powerless to stop it, Chucai sighed, "The people's suffering begins here!"

sentences.zh: 楚材嘗與諸王宴，醉臥車中，帝臨平野見之，直幸其營，登車，手撼之。

translations.literal: Chucai once feasted with the princes, drunkenly sleeping in his carriage; the Emperor came to the open plain and saw him, went straight to his camp, mounted the carriage, and shook him by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast with the princes Chucai fell drunk asleep in his carriage; the emperor saw him on the plain, went straight to his camp, climbed into the carriage, and shook him awake.

sentences.zh: 楚材熟睡未醒，方怒其擾己，忽開目視，始知帝至，驚起謝，帝曰：「有酒獨醉，不與朕同樂耶？」

translations.literal: Chucai was in deep sleep and had not awakened; he was just angry at being disturbed when suddenly he opened his eyes and saw—it was the Emperor who had come; startled, he rose to apologize; the Emperor said, "You have wine and get drunk alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Still asleep, he was about to rebuke whoever disturbed him when he opened his eyes and saw the emperor; he started up in alarm to apologize. The emperor said, "Drinking alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"

sentences.zh: 笑而去。

translations.literal: Laughing, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Laughing, he left.

sentences.zh: 楚材不及冠帶，馳詣行宮，帝為置酒，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: Chucai, without time for cap and belt, galloped to the traveling palace; the Emperor set out wine for him, and they enjoyed themselves to the utmost before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai rode to the traveling palace without even fixing his cap and belt; the emperor set out wine, and they drank together in great delight.

sentences.zh: 楚材當國日久，得祿分其親族，未嘗私以官。

translations.literal: Chucai had long directed the state; he received salary and divided it among his kin, but never privately gave them office.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai had governed for many years, sharing his salary with his kin but never appointing them to office for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 行省劉敏從容言之，楚材曰：「睦親之義，但當資以金帛。

translations.literal: Liu Min of the Branch Secretariat spoke to him at ease; Chucai said, "In the principle of cherishing kin, one should only supply them with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min of the Branch Secretariat raised the matter gently; Chucai said, "Kin should be supported with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 若使從政而違法，吾不能徇私恩也。」

translations.literal: If they are put in government and violate the law, I cannot favor private affection."
translations.idiomatic: If they enter government and break the law, I cannot show private favor."

sentences.zh: 歲辛丑二月三日，帝疾篤，醫言脈已絕。

translations.literal: In the year xinchou, on the third day of the second month, the Emperor's illness was grave; the physicians said his pulse had ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the second month of the xinchou year the emperor fell gravely ill; the physicians said his pulse had failed.

sentences.zh: 皇后不知所為，召楚材問之，對曰：「今任使非人，賣官鬻獄，囚系非辜者多。

translations.literal: The Empress did not know what to do and summoned Chucai to ask; he replied, "Now appointments are of unworthy men, offices are sold and prisons traded, and many innocents are imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress did not know what to do and summoned Chucai; he said, "Unworthy men hold office, offices and judgments are sold, and many innocents languish in prison.

sentences.zh: 古人一言而善，熒惑退舍，請赦天下囚徒。」

translations.literal: In antiquity one good word made Mars withdraw its lodging; I request amnesty for all prisoners under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a single good act made Mars withdraw; I beg that all prisoners under Heaven be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 後即欲行之，楚材曰：「非君命不可。」

translations.literal: The Empress then wished to carry it out at once; Chucai said, "Without the ruler's command it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: The empress wished to act at once; Chucai said, "It cannot be done without the emperor's command."

sentences.zh: 俄頃，帝少蘇，因入奏，請肆赦，帝已不能言，首肯之。

translations.literal: In a moment the Emperor revived slightly; Chucai therefore entered to memorialize and request a general pardon; the Emperor could no longer speak but nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor rallied slightly; Chucai entered and asked for a general amnesty; the emperor could not speak but nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 是夜，醫者候脈復生，適宣讀赦書時也，翌日而瘳。

translations.literal: That night the physicians waited and his pulse returned to life—just as the amnesty edict was being proclaimed; the next day he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the physicians found his pulse return—just as the amnesty was proclaimed; the next day he recovered.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月四日，帝將出獵，楚材以太乙數推之，亟言其不可，左右皆曰：「不騎射，無以為樂。」

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the eleventh month in winter the Emperor was about to go hunting; Chucai calculated by the Taiyi numbers and urgently said it could not be done; those at his side all said, "Without riding and shooting there is no pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the eleventh month the emperor was about to go hunting; Chucai calculated by the Taiyi method and urgently warned against it; his attendants said, "Without riding and shooting, what pleasure is there?"

sentences.zh: 獵五日，帝崩於行在所。

translations.literal: After five days of hunting the Emperor died at the traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: After five days of hunting the emperor died at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后乃馬真氏稱制，崇信姦回，庶政多紊。

translations.literal: The Empress, née Töregene, assumed regency, honored and trusted wicked men, and general administration was much disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Töregene assumed regency, favored wicked men, and civil government fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 奧魯剌合蠻以貨得政柄，廷中悉畏附之。

translations.literal: Oqturqalmish obtained political power through wealth, and everyone in court feared and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Oqturqalmish bought political power with wealth, and the whole court feared and fawned on him.

sentences.zh: 楚材面折廷爭，言人所難言，人皆危之。

translations.literal: Chucai confronted them in court and disputed, speaking what others found hard to speak; all considered him in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai confronted them openly in court, saying what others dared not say, and all feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 癸卯五月，熒惑犯房，楚材奏曰：「當有驚擾，然訖無事。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the year guimao Mars invaded the House constellation; Chucai memorialized, "There will be alarm and disturbance, but in the end nothing will happen."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the guimao year Mars invaded the House constellation; Chucai memorialized, "There will be alarm, but in the end no harm."

sentences.zh: 居無何，朝廷用兵，事起倉卒，後遂令授甲選腹心，至欲西遷以避之。

translations.literal: Before long the court took up arms; the affair arose in haste; later they ordered armor issued and trusted men selected, even wishing to move the capital west to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court mobilized for war in sudden alarm; armor was issued, trusted men chosen, and some even proposed moving the capital west to escape.

sentences.zh: 楚材進曰：「朝廷天下根本，根本一搖，天下將亂。

translations.literal: Chucai advanced and said, "The court is the root of all under Heaven; if the root is shaken, all under Heaven will fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The court is the root of the realm; shake the root and the realm will fall into chaos.

sentences.zh: 臣觀天道，必無患也。」

translations.literal: I observe Heaven's Way—there will surely be no calamity."
translations.idiomatic: I read Heaven's signs—there will be no real danger."

sentences.zh: 後數日乃定。

translations.literal: After several days it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 後以御寶空紙付奧都剌合蠻，使自書填行之。

translations.literal: Later blank sheets bearing the imperial seal were given to Oqturqalmish, allowing him to write and fill them in himself for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Later blank sheets bearing the imperial seal were handed to Oqturqalmish so he could write and execute edicts at will.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「天下者先帝之天下。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "All under Heaven is the late Emperor's Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The realm belongs to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷自有憲章，今欲紊之，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: The court has its own statutes; to disorder them now—I dare not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: The court has its own laws; to throw them into confusion—I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 事遂止。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又有旨：「凡奧都剌合蠻所建白，令史不為書者，斷其手。」

translations.literal: There was again an order: "For all proposals made by Oqturqalmish, if a clerk does not write them down, his hand is to be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Another order followed: "Any clerk who refused to record Oqturqalmish's proposals was to have his hand cut off."

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「國之典故，先帝悉委老臣，令史何與焉？

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The state's precedents—the late Emperor wholly entrusted them to this old minister; what have clerks to do with them?
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "State precedent was entrusted entirely to me by the late emperor—what business is it of the clerks?

sentences.zh: 事若合理，自當奉行，如不可行，死且不避，況截手乎！」

translations.literal: If a matter is reasonable, it should naturally be carried out; if it cannot be done, I would not avoid death—how much less the cutting off of hands!"
translations.idiomatic: If a proposal is sound I will carry it out; if not, I would not shrink from death—still less from losing a hand!"

sentences.zh: 后不悅。

translations.literal: The Empress was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was displeased.

sentences.zh: 楚材辨論不已，因大聲曰：「老臣事太祖、太宗三十餘年，無負于國，皇后亦豈能無罪殺臣也！」

translations.literal: Chucai argued without cease and therefore said loudly, "This old minister served Taizu and Taizong for more than thirty years without failing the state—the Empress also surely cannot kill me without cause!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai would not stop arguing and cried out, "I served Taizu and Taizong for more than thirty years without failing the state—the empress cannot kill me without cause!"

sentences.zh: 後雖憾之，亦以先朝舊勳，深敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Though the Empress resented him, because he was an old merit-holder of the former court she deeply respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Though she resented him, she deeply respected and feared him as a veteran of the former reigns.

sentences.zh: 甲辰夏五月，薨於位，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the year jiachen he died in office, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the jiachen year he died in office at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 皇后哀悼，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The Empress mourned him and gave funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The empress mourned him and gave lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 後有譖楚材者，言其在相位日久，天下貢賦，半入其家。

translations.literal: Later someone slandered Chucai, saying that during his long tenure in the chief ministership half of the realm's tribute and levies entered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone slandered him, claiming that during his long tenure half the empire's revenues had gone into his household.

sentences.zh: 後命近臣麻里扎覆視之，唯琴阮十餘，及古今書畫、金石、遺文數千卷。

translations.literal: The Empress ordered the close attendant Malizha to re-inspect; there were only a dozen or so qins and ruan, and several thousand scrolls of ancient and modern calligraphy and painting, metal and stone inscriptions, and surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ordered the intimate Malizha to inspect his estate and found only a dozen musical instruments and several thousand scrolls of books, paintings, and inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，贈經國議制寅亮佐運功臣、太師、上柱國，追封廣寧王，諡文正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously given the title Merit-holder Who Deliberates on State Regulation with Vigorous Brilliance and Assists the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Guangning, with the temple name Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, with the posthumous name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 子鉉、鑄。

translations.literal: His sons were Xian and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xian and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 鑄字成仲，幼聰敏，善屬文，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: Zhu, styled Chengzhong, was clever as a child, skilled in literary composition, and especially adept at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, courtesy name Chengzhong, was clever as a child, skilled at writing, and especially adept at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 楚材薨，嗣領中書省事，時年二十三。

translations.literal: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded to direct the affairs of the Secretariat; at the time he was twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded him as head of the Secretariat at the age of twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 鑄上言宜疏禁網，遂採歷代德政合於時宜者八十一章以進。

translations.literal: Zhu memorialized that the prohibitions of the law should be loosened, and thereupon collected eighty-one items of benevolent government from successive ages suited to the times and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu memorialized that the laws should be eased and presented eighty-one examples of benevolent governance from past dynasties suited to the present.

sentences.zh: 戊午，憲宗徵蜀，詔鑄領侍衛驍果以從，屢出奇計，攻下城邑，賜以尚方金鎖甲及內厩驄馬。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu Emperor Xianzong campaigned against Shu; Zhu was ordered to lead the palace guard swift troops in attendance; he repeatedly devised surprising stratagems, captured walled cities, and was bestowed imperial gold-linked armor and piebald horses from the inner stables.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year, when Emperor Xianzong campaigned in Shu, Zhu led the palace guard; his repeated stratagems took cities, and he was rewarded with imperial armor and piebald horses from the royal stables.

sentences.zh: 乙未，憲宗崩，阿里不哥叛，鑄棄妻子，挺身自朔方來歸，世祖嘉其忠，即日召見，賞賜優厚。
