translations.literal: In the year yiwei Emperor Xianzong died; Ariq Böke rebelled; Zhu abandoned wife and children and came alone from the northern frontier to submit; Emperor Shizu praised his loyalty, summoned him that same day, and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year, when Emperor Xianzong died and Ariq Böke rebelled, Zhu abandoned his family and came alone from the north to submit; Kublai praised his loyalty, received him that day, and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed left chief director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，詔將兵備禦北邊，後徵兵扈從，敗阿里不哥於上都之北。

translations.literal: That winter he was ordered to command troops to guard the northern frontier; later he was summoned with the army in attendance and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was ordered to guard the northern frontier; later he joined the imperial campaign and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 奏定法令三十七章，吏民便之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and fixed thirty-seven chapters of laws and regulations, to the convenience of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and codified thirty-seven chapters of law, to the benefit of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 二年，行省山東。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as Branch Secretariat of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served as branch secretariat of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未幾徵還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 初，清廟雅樂，止有登歌，詔鑄制宮懸八佾之舞。

translations.literal: Earlier, for the refined music of the Imperial Temple there was only the ascending song; Zhu was ordered to compose the palace ensemble and the dance of eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the imperial temple music had only the ascending hymns; Zhu was ordered to compose the full court orchestra and the eight-row dance.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，樂舞成，表上之，仍請賜名《大成》，制曰「可」。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the fourth year the music and dance were completed; he memorialized and presented them, and also requested the bestowed name "Great Completion"; the decree said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year the music and dance were completed; he presented them and asked that they be named "Great Completion"; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 六月，改榮祿大夫、平章政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Associate Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and associate administrator of affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，復拜光祿大夫、中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and left chief director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Associate Administrator of Important Military and Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made associate administrator of important military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔監修國史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，必諮訪焉。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs, it invariably consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: On great matters of state the court always consulted him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed Left Chief Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed left chief director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬十月，坐不納職印、妄奏東平人聚謀為逆、間諜幕僚、及黨罪囚阿里沙，遂罷免，仍沒其家貲之半，徙居山後。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the twentieth year, on charges of not accepting the seal of office, falsely memorializing that people of Dongping had gathered to plot rebellion, spying through staff, and shielding the guilty prisoner Alisha, he was dismissed, half his household property was confiscated, and he was moved to live behind the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he was dismissed for refusing his seal of office, falsely reporting a Dongping conspiracy, employing spies among his staff, and shielding the prisoner Alisha; half his property was confiscated and he was exiled north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子十一人：希徵，希勃，希亮，希寬，希素，希固，希周，希光，希逸淮東宣慰使，餘失其名。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, Xiyi (Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong)—the rest have lost their names.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, and Xiyi, who became pacification commissioner of Huaidong; the names of the rest are lost.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，贈推忠保德宣力佐治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、懿寧王，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously given the title Merit-holder Who Promotes Loyalty, Preserves Virtue, and Expands Strength in Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Prince of Yining, with the temple name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and Prince of Yining, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: ○粘合重山子南合

translations.literal: Nianhe Zhongshan; his son Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhe Zhongshan, with an account of his son Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 粘合重山，金源貴族也。

translations.literal: Nianhe Zhongshan was a noble of the Jin source.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhe Zhongshan was a noble of the Jin imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 國初為質子，知金將亡，遂委質焉。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was a hostage; knowing that Jin was about to perish, he then pledged himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years he served as a hostage; seeing that Jin was doomed, he pledged himself to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜畜馬四百匹，使為宿衛官必阇赤。

translations.literal: Taizu bestowed four hundred horses for raising and made him a guard officer, a beküchi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu granted him four hundred horses and appointed him a palace guard, a beküchi.

sentences.zh: 從平諸國有功。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the various states and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the realms and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 圍涼州，執大旗指麾六軍，手中流矢，不動。

translations.literal: Besieging Liangzhou, he held the great banner and directed the six armies; an arrow struck his hand, yet he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Liangzhou he held the great banner and directed the armies; when an arrow struck his hand he did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 已而為侍從官，數得侍宴內廷。

translations.literal: Later he became an attendant officer and several times attended banquets in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He later became an attendant and often joined banquets in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 因諫曰：「臣聞天子以天下為憂，憂之未有不治，忘憂未有能治者也。

translations.literal: He therefore remonstrated, saying, "I have heard that the Son of Heaven takes all under Heaven as his worry; where there is worry there has never been failure to govern, and where worry is forgotten there has never been successful governance.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated, "I have heard that a ruler who worries for the realm never fails to govern it, and one who forgets that worry never succeeds.

sentences.zh: 置酒為樂，此忘憂之術也。」

translations.literal: Setting out wine for pleasure—this is the method of forgetting worry."
translations.idiomatic: Feasting for pleasure is the way to forget such worry."

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 立中書省，以重山有積勳，授左丞相。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat was established, because Zhongshan had accumulated merit he was appointed Left Chief Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was established, Zhongshan was appointed left chief director in recognition of his long service.

sentences.zh: 時耶律楚材為右丞相，凡建官立法，任賢使能，與夫分郡邑，定課賦，通漕運，足國用，多出楚材，而重山佐成之。

translations.literal: At the time Yelü Chucai was Right Chief Director; in establishing offices and making laws, appointing the worthy and employing the capable, as well as dividing commanderies and districts, fixing levies and taxes, opening grain transport by water, and filling state revenues—most came from Chucai, while Zhongshan assisted and completed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Chucai was right chief director at the time; most of the work of establishing offices, appointing talent, dividing commanderies, fixing taxes, opening grain transport, and filling the treasury came from Chucai, with Zhongshan assisting him.

sentences.zh: 太宗七年，從伐宋，詔軍前行中書省事，許以便宜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taizong he followed the campaign against Song; he was ordered to conduct Secretariat affairs before the army, with discretionary authority permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's seventh year he joined the campaign against Song and was ordered to handle Secretariat affairs with the army, with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 師入宋境，江淮州邑望風款附，重山降其民三十餘萬，取定城、天長二邑，不誅一人。

translations.literal: When the army entered Song territory, prefectures and districts along the Yangzi and Huai submitted at the wind's report; Zhongshan caused more than three hundred thousand of their people to surrender, took the two districts of Dingcheng and Tianchang, and killed not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: As the army entered Song territory, cities along the Yangzi and Huai submitted; Zhongshan received the surrender of more than three hundred thousand people, took Dingcheng and Tianchang, and killed no one.

sentences.zh: 復入中書視事，賜中厩馬十匹、貫珠袍一。

translations.literal: He returned to the Secretariat to attend to affairs and was bestowed ten horses from the central stables and one pearl-strung robe.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Secretariat and was rewarded with ten horses from the imperial stables and a pearl-strung robe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，封魏國公，諡忠武。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the temple name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔其子江淮安撫使南合嗣行軍前中書省事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered his son Nanhe, Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner, to succeed to Secretariat affairs before the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict ordered his son Nanhe, Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner, to succeed to Secretariat affairs with the army.

sentences.zh: 時大將察罕圍壽春，七日始下，欲屠其城，南合曰：「不降者獨守將耳，其民何罪？」

translations.literal: At the time the great general Chaghan besieged Shouchun and took it only after seven days; he wished to slaughter the city. Nanhe said, "Only the defending commander refused to surrender—what crime have the people committed?"
translations.idiomatic: When the great general Chaghan besieged Shouchun and took it only after seven days, he wished to massacre the city. Nanhe said, "Only the commander refused to surrender—what crime have the people committed?"

sentences.zh: 由是獲免。

translations.literal: The city was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: The people were thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖伐宋軍于汴，南合進曰：「李璮承國厚恩，坐制一方，然其人多詐，叛無日矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shizu campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe advanced and said, "Li Tan has received deep favor from the state and controls a region on his own, yet his people are full of deceit—rebellion is only a matter of time."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kublai campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe said, "Li Tan has received great favor from the state and holds a region on his own, yet his followers are treacherous—rebellion is only a matter of time."

sentences.zh: 帝亦患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled too.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，兩遷宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was twice transferred as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was twice promoted as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，授中書右丞、中興等路行中書省事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat and put in charge of Secretariat affairs for the Zhongxing circuit and other routes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat and put in charge of Secretariat affairs for Zhongxing and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷秦蜀五路四川行中書省事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to oversee Secretariat affairs for the five Qin-Shu circuits of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to oversee Secretariat affairs for the five Qin-Shu circuits of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 其年，李璮反益都，帝使諭南合曰：「卿言猶在耳，璮果反矣。

translations.literal: That year Li Tan rebelled at Yidu; the emperor sent word to Nanhe, saying, "Your words are still in my ears—Tan has indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Tan rebelled at Yidu; the emperor sent word to Nanhe, "Your warning is still in my ears—Tan has rebelled as you said.

sentences.zh: 卿宜謹守西鄙。」

translations.literal: You should diligently guard the western frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Guard the western frontier carefully."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣謹受詔，不敢以西鄙為陛下憂。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject respectfully accepts the edict and dares not trouble Your Majesty over the western marches."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I accept the edict and will not trouble Your Majesty over the western marches."

sentences.zh: 明年，授中書平章政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed grand councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed grand councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，病卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 封魏國公，諡宣昭。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Xuanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous name Xuanzhao.

sentences.zh: 子博溫察兒，知河中府。

translations.literal: His son Bowencha'er served as prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bowencha'er served as prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: ○楊惟中

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong.

sentences.zh: 楊惟中，字彥誠，弘州人。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong, styled Yancheng, was a man of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong, courtesy name Yancheng, was a native of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 金末，以孤童子事太宗，知讀書，有膽略，太宗器之。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, as a solitary youth he served Taizong; he knew how to read and had courage and resource; Taizong valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin he served Taizong as a young orphan; he could read, showed courage and resource, and Taizong valued him.

sentences.zh: 年二十，奉命使西域三十餘國，宣暢國威，敷布政條，俾皆籍戶口屬吏，乃歸，帝於是有大用意。

translations.literal: At twenty he was ordered on mission to more than thirty states of the Western Regions, proclaiming national might and spreading administrative regulations, causing all to register households and submit to officials; when he returned, the Emperor thereafter had great designs.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was sent on embassy to more than thirty states of the Western Regions, proclaiming imperial might and imposing registration of households; on his return the emperor formed great plans for the realm.

sentences.zh: 皇子闊出伐宋，命惟中於軍前行中書省事。

translations.literal: When Prince Kuochu campaigned against Song, Weizhong was ordered to conduct Secretariat affairs before the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kuochu campaigned against Song, Weizhong was ordered to handle Secretariat affairs with the army.

sentences.zh: 克宋棗陽、光化等軍，光、隨、郢、復等州，及襄陽、德安府，凡得名士數十人，收伊、洛諸書送燕都，立宋大儒周惇頤祠，建太極書院，延儒士趙復、王粹等講授其間，遂通聖賢學，慨然欲以道濟天下。

translations.literal: He captured the Song garrisons of Zaoyang, Guanghua, and others, the prefectures of Guang, Sui, Ying, Fu, and others, and the prefectures of Xiangyang and De'an; in all he obtained several tens of eminent scholars, collected books of the Yi and Luo regions and sent them to the Yan capital, established a shrine to the great Song Confucian Zhou Dunyi, built the Taiji Academy, and invited Confucian scholars Zhao Fu, Wang Cui, and others to lecture there; thereby the learning of the sages was opened, and he sighed with resolve to save the world through the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Zaoyang, Guanghua, and other garrisons and the prefectures of Guang, Sui, Ying, Fu, Xiangyang, and De'an; he gathered dozens of eminent scholars, sent books from the Yi and Luo regions to Yan, built a shrine to Zhou Dunyi and the Taiji Academy, and invited Zhao Fu, Wang Cui, and others to lecture there, opening the way to sage learning and resolving to save the world through the Way.

sentences.zh: 拜中書令，太宗崩，太后稱制，惟中以一相負任天下。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat; when Taizong died and the Empress Dowager assumed regency, Weizhong as a single chief minister bore responsibility for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Secretariat; when Taizong died and the empress dowager assumed regency, Weizhong bore the weight of the realm as sole chief minister.

sentences.zh: 定宗即位，平陽道斷事官斜徹橫恣不法，詔惟中宣慰，惟中按誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, the judicial officer of Pingyang Circuit, Cheqie, was violent and lawless; Weizhong was ordered to pacify and comfort; he investigated and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, Cheqie, judicial officer of Pingyang Circuit, ruled lawlessly; Weizhong was sent to pacify the region and had him executed after investigation.

sentences.zh: 金亡，其將武仙潰於鄧州，餘黨散入太原、真定間，據大明川，用金開興年號，眾至數万，剽掠數千里，詔會諸道兵討之，不克。

translations.literal: When Jin perished, its general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou; the remnant band scattered between Taiyuan and Zhending, occupied Damingchuan, used Jin's Kaixing reign title, numbered tens of thousands, and plundered for several thousand li; an edict gathered troops from all circuits to attack them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin fell, the general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou; remnants scattered between Taiyuan and Zhending, seized Damingchuan, used the Jin Kaixing reign title, and numbered tens of thousands, plundering for thousands of li; troops from all circuits failed to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 惟中仗節開諭，降其渠帥，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Weizhong, bearing his staff, opened persuasion; their chieftains surrendered and the remnant band was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong went with imperial authority to persuade them; their leaders surrendered and the remnant was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，世祖以太弟鎮金蓮川，得開府，專封拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Shizu as the senior imperial brother garrisoned Jinlianchuan, obtained the right to open a government office, and had exclusive authority to appoint and enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Kublai as senior imperial brother garrisoned Jinlianchuan with authority to open his own office and make appointments independently.

sentences.zh: 乃立河南道經略司於汴梁，奏惟中等為使，俾屯田唐、鄧、申、裕、嵩、汝、蔡、息、亳、潁諸州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established the Henan Circuit Pacification Commission at Bianliang, memorialized Weizhong and others as commissioners, and ordered garrison farming in the prefectures of Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Henan Circuit Pacification Commission at Bianliang, appointed Weizhong commissioner, and ordered garrison farming in Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 初，滅金時，以監河橋萬戶劉福為河南道總管，福貪鄙殘酷，虐害遺民二十餘年。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jin was destroyed, the ten-thousand-household chief Liu Fu, overseer of the river bridge, was made Henan Circuit commander; Fu was greedy, base, and cruel, abusing and harming the surviving people for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was destroyed, Liu Fu, overseer of the river bridge, was made commander of Henan Circuit; greedy and cruel, he abused the surviving people for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 惟中至，召福聽約束，福稱疾不至，惟中設大梃於坐，復召之，使謂福曰：「汝不奉命，吾以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: When Weizhong arrived, he summoned Fu to hear his orders of restraint; Fu claimed illness and did not come; Weizhong set a great staff by his seat and summoned him again, sending word to Fu, "If you do not obey the command, I will deal with you by military law."
translations.idiomatic: When Weizhong arrived he summoned Fu to receive orders; Fu claimed illness and refused to come; Weizhong placed a heavy staff beside his seat and sent word: "If you disobey, I will deal with you by military law."

sentences.zh: 福不得已，以數千人擁衛見惟中，惟中即握大梃擊僕之。

translations.literal: Fu had no choice; with several thousand men escorting him he came to see Weizhong; Weizhong immediately seized the great staff and struck him down.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had no choice but to come with several thousand guards; Weizhong seized the staff and struck him down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 數日福死，河南大治。

translations.literal: Within several days Fu died, and Henan was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu died within days, and Henan was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 遷陝右四川宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi Right and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍帥橫侈病民，郭千戶者尤甚，殺人之夫而奪其妻，惟中戮之以徇，關中肅然。

translations.literal: At the time the various army commanders were overbearing and extravagant, harming the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was especially so, killing a man's husband and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and Guanzhong was solemnly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Army commanders were oppressing the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was worst of all, killing a man and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and the region was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 語人曰：「吾非好殺，國家綱紀不立，致此輩賊害良民，無所控告，雖慾不去，可乎！」

translations.literal: He told others, "I am not fond of killing; the state's discipline is not established, causing men like these to harm good people with nowhere to appeal; though I wish not to remove them, can it be done!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I do not love killing, but when discipline fails and such men prey on the innocent with no recourse, how can I leave them unpunished?"

sentences.zh: 歲己未，世祖總統東師，奏惟中為江淮京湖南北路宣撫使，俾建行台，以先啟行，宣布恩信，蒙古、漢軍諸帥並聽節制。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei Shizu commanded the eastern army; he memorialized Weizhong as Pacification Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jinghu, and North and South circuits, ordered him to establish a traveling office, go ahead to open the campaign, proclaim grace and trust, and all Mongol and Han army commanders were to obey his control.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year Kublai commanded the eastern army and appointed Weizhong pacification commissioner of the Jianghuai and Jinghu circuits, with authority to establish a traveling office, advance ahead to proclaim imperial grace, and command all Mongol and Han generals.

sentences.zh: 師還，卒於蔡州，年五十五。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he died at Caizhou, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he died at Caizhou at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，追諡曰忠肅公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the temple name Duke Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously honored as Duke Zhongsu.
